purpose: Turn one simulation run's action ledger into a single event-level escalation/calming prediction that the existing evaluation schema can consume.

uses_only: cutoff-eligible case snapshot (cutoff, source version, source records)
the run's persisted action ledger and its per-agent runtime message references
the run's persisted final local state, whose limitation is stated under known_data_limits
the run's own configuration (agent_count, rounds, seed, cutoff, source_version)
never_uses: evaluation-only inputs or any future outcome series
freeze_declaration.order: This rule set is fixed before any outcome or label is read. The adapter records the hash of this document in its freeze record so the rule that produced a prediction cannot be changed afterwards without breaking the hash.
freeze_declaration.note: A prediction produced by this method is simulation-derived. It is not a baseline, and a baseline result must never be reported as this method's result.

escalating: action is share, comment or express_complaint_intent, AND (the action cites at least one runtime message OR it cites no cutoff-eligible source evidence)
the agent's persisted final local emotion state is at or below negative_emotion_threshold
calming: action is observe or seek_clarification, AND it cites cutoff-eligible source evidence, AND it does not cite a runtime message
undecided: the agent's row for the selected round is not valid, so it carries no decision to classify
the row is valid but matches neither condition above; the method does not claim it either way
per_agent_classification.precedence: escalating conditions are evaluated first; an agent matching any escalating condition is classified escalating even if it also matches a calming condition

known_data_limits.per_round_state_is_not_persisted: The engine writes a memory row carrying the action and its reason, then updates the local emotion state afterwards, so a per-round emotion snapshot cannot be recovered from the ledger. The emotion condition therefore reads the run's persisted FINAL state. It is a final-state condition applied to the agents of the selected round, not a reconstruction of that round's state, and the prediction must never be described as resting on a per-round state snapshot.
known_data_limits.consequence: In a run whose emotion drifts across rounds, that condition can fire on agents of an earlier round because of a later round. The action conditions are round-local and unaffected. Recorded here so a reviewer weighs it instead of discovering it.

aggregation.universe: every agent that produced a valid decision in the selected round
aggregation.escalation_share: count(escalating) / count(universe), rounded to 6 decimal places
aggregation.label_rule: escalation when escalation_share >= escalation_share_threshold, otherwise calming
aggregation.undecided_handling: rows that are not valid are excluded from the universe and counted separately; they never contribute to the share

admission_conditions.note: These qualify how a label may be used. They are not part of the classification rule, so applying them does not change any label and therefore does not change the method version.
formal_direction_prediction: the run is complete and its last completed round is the configured last round, so the persisted final state the rule reads is the state at the end of the predicted round
the event carries exactly one direction prediction in the set that would be scored, counting every source
the prediction is frozen, with the run selected, before any outcome or label is read
tentative_only: the run is partial: the label may still be computed and is reported with qualification tentative_partial_run, but it is refused by the formal preflight and must be labelled as tentative analysis wherever it is shown
separate_reports: a simulation-derived prediction and a model baseline are separate reports and are never pooled into one event
a baseline result must never be reported as this method's result, and this method's result must never be reported as a baseline's

method_limits: The rule reads the simulation's own action vocabulary and local state. It is not calibrated against any observed event trajectory.
It is deterministic for a given ledger, so an identical ledger always yields the same label; it carries no confidence or probability.
It produces a direction label only. It makes no sentiment claim, and sentiment must be predicted separately if it is predicted at all.
A simulation run of a synthetic or fictional case yields a synthetic-data prediction; such a case is excluded from formal denominators by the evaluator itself.
